name: Liability Waiver
description: A general activity liability waiver: participant details, emergency contact, assumption of risk and release, typed name and consent.
seoDescription: Liability waiver template for activities and events. Collects participant details, minor info, emergency contact, assumption of risk, typed name and consent.
thumbnailAlt: Liability Waiver form beside a photo of two adults kayaking on a flowing river, enjoying outdoor leisure activities in summer

content.intro: A liability waiver is a form in which a participant acknowledges the risks of an activity, releases the organizer from certain claims, and gives an emergency contact, so the organizer has a record of informed agreement before the activity starts. This template uses plain-language sample terms, a typed full name and a single consent box, and it covers adults signing for themselves or a parent signing for a minor.
content.audience: Adventure and outdoor operators, fitness classes, event organizers, rental businesses, clubs and volunteer programs.
useCases: Kayak, climbing or trampoline park check-in
Fun runs, obstacle races and charity sports events
Equipment rental such as bikes or paddleboards
tips: Treat the waiver text as a starting point and have it reviewed by a lawyer for your local rules before you use it.
Show the waiver as a QR code at check-in so participants complete it on their phone before the activity.
Turn on a PDF template to create a filled waiver PDF for each response, and send the participant an email copy.

faq.question: What should a liability waiver include?
faq.answer: The participant's name, date of birth and contact details; the activity and date; a clear description of the risks; an assumption of risk and release of claims; permission for emergency medical treatment; an emergency contact; and the participant's typed name, date and agreement. For minors, add the parent or guardian's details.

faq.question: Is a typed name on an online waiver binding?
faq.answer: In many places a typed name plus a clear consent box can show agreement, but whether a waiver holds up depends on local law, the wording and the activity. Waivers usually cannot excuse gross negligence. Have yours reviewed by a lawyer for your local rules.

faq.question: Can a parent sign a waiver for a child?
faq.answer: Parents commonly complete waivers for minors, but courts in some states and countries do not enforce a parent's release of a child's future claims. Check your local rules and insurer's guidance.

faq.question: How long should I keep signed waivers?
faq.answer: Many organizers keep them at least as long as the time limit for injury claims where they operate, often several years and longer for minors. Responses stay in your account, and you can export them to Excel or CSV for your records.

fields.label: Who is completing this waiver?
options: A parent or legal guardian of a participant under 18

fields.label: Parent or guardian full name
fields.hint: Only if the participant is under 18

fields.label: Medical conditions or injuries staff should know about

fields.content:
Assumption of risk. I understand this activity involves risks, including falls, collisions, equipment failure, weather and the actions of others, which may cause injury, illness or property damage. I take part voluntarily and accept these risks.

Release. To the extent allowed by law, I release the organizer, its staff and volunteers from claims arising from my participation, except claims caused by their gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Rules and medical care. I will follow safety instructions and use the equipment provided. I confirm I am fit to take part and authorize emergency medical treatment if needed.

fields.label: Type your full name
fields.hint: Participant, or parent or guardian if under 18

fields.label: Agreement
options: I have read and understood this waiver and I agree to its terms
